question: Which of the following drugs obtained by means of molecular engineering techniques is not applicable in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Infliximab" -> "TNF-alpha inhibitor" -> "reduces inflammation" -> "used in rheumatoid arthritis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Denosumab" -> "RANKL inhibitor" -> "reduces bone resorption" -> "used in osteoporosis" -> "not typically used in rheumatoid arthritis" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Adalimumab" -> "TNF-alpha inhibitor" -> "reduces inflammation" -> "used in rheumatoid arthritis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Anakinra" -> "IL-1 receptor antagonist" -> "reduces inflammation" -> "used in rheumatoid arthritis" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Etanercept" -> "TNF-alpha inhibitor" -> "reduces inflammation" -> "used in rheumatoid arthritis" -> 90%
analysis: Infliximab, Adalimumab, Anakinra, and Etanercept are all used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis. Denosumab, however, is primarily used for conditions related to bone density, such as osteoporosis, and is not typically used for rheumatoid arthritis.
